ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Maia the bee can only walk on colorful houses. How many ways can you color exactly three white houses with the same color so that Maia can walk from $A$ to $B$ ?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: Looking at the attached hexagon-house picture, the pink/colorful houses form two disconnected colorful components. On the left, L consists of A and the two lower pink houses. On the right, R consists of the top pink house, the upper-right pink house, and B. There are six white houses between these components. Label them as follows: w1 is the white house just upper-right of A; w2 is the upper white house left of the top pink house; w3 is the central-left white house; w4 is the central-right white house below the top pink house; w5 is the lower-middle white house; w6 is the rightmost white house touching the B side. From the shared sides in the image, L touches w1, w3, w5, and R touches w2, w4, w6. The white-white shared-side adjacencies are w1-w2, w1-w3, w2-w3, w2-w4, w3-w4, w3-w5, w4-w5, w4-w6, and w5-w6. Reasoning: Coloring exactly three white houses selects a triple from the six white houses, so there are C(6,3)=20 possible triples. Maia can walk from A to B exactly when the selected white houses contain a connected component that touches both L and R. Count the complement. The failing triples are {w1,w3,w5}, which only touches L; {w2,w4,w6}, which only touches R; {w1,w3,w6}, where the L-side component w1-w3 is not connected to w6; and {w1,w4,w6}, where w4-w6 is on the R side and w1 is separated on the L side. Thus the number of successful triples is 20-4=16. Final answer: 16
